findings.failure_mode: Missing file, permission error, or unreadable path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> or a typed domain error and use ? to propagate

findings.failure_mode: Corrupted or malformed CSV data aborts the program instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use .map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid) or equivalent typed error and return Result<Vec<Record>, E>

findings.problem: Lossy u32-to-u16 cast via `as u16` silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: A u32 value in range 65536..=4294967295 silently wraps to a wrong u16, corrupting data with no error
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) or parse directly as u16 with .map_err

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses the Vec by index without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: A line with fewer than one comma (or empty line) panics with index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and match on the two-option result, or use parts.get(0)

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses the Vec by index without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: A line with exactly one comma but no second field panics with index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and match on the two-option result, or use parts.get(1)

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is I/O side-effect inside the data-processing pipeline
findings.failure_mode: Pure computation is contaminated with logging; breaks determinism, makes testing harder, and leaks the imperative shell into the core
findings.fix: Remove println! from the map closure. If logging is needed, push log messages as data and flush them in the shell layer after the pure transformation completes

findings.problem: Record uses raw String for name instead of a typed newtype like RecordName
findings.failure_mode: Any string is accepted as a record name; domain invariants (e.g., non-empty, no whitespace) are not enforced at the type level
findings.fix: Define a newtype struct RecordName(String) with a fallible constructor that enforces invariants; use it in Record

findings.problem: No try_reserve or allocation budget on the intermediate Vec<String> or final Vec<Record>
findings.failure_mode: Maliciously large input can exhaust heap memory before any validation occurs; allocation failure is unhandled
findings.fix: Estimate max lines, call try_reserve on the output Vec before collecting, and map allocation failure to a typed Allocation error

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string is a blocking I/O call directly in a pub function that appears to be a data-loading utility
findings.failure_mode: The function is not pure but also does not express its I/O nature in its return type; callers cannot distinguish I/O failures from data errors
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, ShardsError> where ShardsError variants include Io(io::Error), Parse(ParseError), Overflow, and Empty

findings.problem: Collecting all split parts into Vec<String> instead of using split_once for a two-field CSV
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocations per line (each part gets a new String), higher memory pressure, and no benefit over split_once which yields two &str slices
findings.fix: Use `let (name_str, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(…)`, parse directly from the &str slices, and avoid Vec<String> allocation per line

findings.problem: No custom error enum; errors are collapsed into panic via unwrap()
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot programmatically distinguish between file-not-found, parse-invalid, overflow, and empty-input errors
findings.fix: Define an enum ShardsError { Io(io::Error), Invalid, Overflow, Empty } and return Result<Vec<Record>, ShardsError>

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for load_shards performance claim or baseline
findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify whether this allocation-heavy implementation meets performance requirements
findings.fix: Add a criterion or similar benchmark measuring throughput and allocation for typical and adversarial inputs

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_shards throughput or allocation behavior
no profiler evidence (flamegraph/callopt) to identify hot paths
no allocation tracing (e.g., dhat, or --report-time) to verify allocation budget
no second-ring validation (Miri/UB checks) for unsafe or pointer behavior in the crate
no command-level CLI wrapper or entry-point evidence for end-to-end behavior
residual_risk: Static review only with no commands run. All unwrap() sites, unchecked indexing, lossy casts, and hidden I/O in the core are confirmed blockers that must be fixed before delivery. The function as written will panic on any malformed input, missing file, or value overflow. A full typed error taxonomy, split_once-based parsing, try_from conversions, removal of println! from the pipeline, and bounded allocation are required before the code meets Holzman Rust standards.
